We've seen the warnings from informational videos over the decades , and our personal blunders and experiences have demonstrated this point, too .
We can, of course, be attentive behind the wheel, but that doesn't account for the others who aren't while on the road.
It's partly why dash cams and their resulting videos have gained so much traction in recent years.

Dispatches and field testing reports from Cartoq.com highlight pivotal updates regarding Indian Passenger Vehicle, bringing crucial technical, pricing, and real-world ownership data to prospective buyers.

Under real-world Indian driving conditions, certified ARAI fuel economy claims often diverge significantly from day-to-day driving numbers. While factory lab tests routinely claim 17 to 20 kmpl, bumper-to-bumper city traffic with active air conditioning typically yields between 10.5 and 13.2 kmpl for turbo-petrol powertrains, and 14.5 to 16.8 kmpl for refined diesel iterations. Highway cruising at steady speeds of 90 kmph allows these engines to settle into their peak thermal efficiency band.

Beyond raw horsepower and torque metrics, daily usability reveals subtle compromises that glossy dealership brochures rarely highlight. When evaluated against primary segment contenders—including the Tata Nexon, Mahindra Thar Roxx, Scorpio-N, Hyundai Creta, and Maruti Brezza—each platform offers distinct mechanical trade-offs. Ladder-frame SUVs deliver bulletproof rough-road durability at the expense of city ride suppleness, whereas monocoque crossovers excel in agile highway manners and effortless urban parking maneuverability.

Our definitive buyer guidance: identify your primary driving pattern before signing a booking form. If your monthly usage exceeds 1,500 kilometers with extensive highway travel, modern BS6.2-compliant diesels and strong hybrid powertrains offer unbeatable operating economics. For city commutes under 30 kilometers daily, a refined turbo-petrol or pure electric derivative delivers the smoothest driving experience.

raw_summary: Back in 2010, Chevrolet introduced the groundbreaking Volt — America's first plug-in hybrid production car. Packing a fairly big 16-kWh battery pack, the Volt had an EPA-estimated electric range of 35 miles, with later first-generation models rated at up to 38 miles. When the battery was depleted, it turned to a 1.4-liter four-cylinder engine with 84 horsepower to cover longer distances. Although it ultimately failed to attract enough buyers and was discontinued in 2019, the Chevrolet Volt was so far ahead of its time that many current PHEVs struggle to match its electric range. In fact, out of the 12 plug-in hybrids with the longest electric-only range on sale right now, four have lower range figures. Of course, many modern PHEVs offer more EV range, with some models, like the 2027 Land Rover Range Rover Plug-in Hybrid, 2027 Mercedes-Benz GLC 350e 4MATIC, and 2027 Toyota RAV4 Plug-in Hybrid, capable of delivering 50 miles of driving without calling on the internal combustion engine.

raw_title: 5 Generations Of The Chevy Impala SS Ranked From Best To Worst Horsepower Ratings
title: 5 Generations Of The Chevy Impala SS Ranked From Best To Worst Horsepower Ratings
raw_summary: Mention a Chevy Impala, and thoughts of an unremarkable family sedan may come to mind, but add an SS next to the nameplate and things change. The Impala SS (Super Sport) is a pure horsepower play that dates back to 1961, two years after the Bowtie brand launched the Impala as a standalone model. Its numbers are still impressive, even by 21st-century standards. The retail version of the Impala SS from the 1960s, which covered two generations, produced up to 425 horsepower. The later Impala SS generations from the 1990s and 2000s were less brutish, offering between 240 and 303 hp, but they were still a step up from their more mundane counterparts. However, these horsepower numbers come with a catch. The output figures for 1960s Impala SS models reflected gross horsepower ratings, which generally didn't account for intake, exhaust, and accessory loads. When the 1970s rolled around, the auto industry was dealing with tighter emissions regulations and insurance companies that took a dim view of high-powered cars. By the 1972 model year, Detroit switched to net horsepower calculations to better reflect real-world engine configurations. Because gross horsepower ratings often varied from manufacturer to manufacturer, there's no standard way to convert horsepower ratings between the methods, but both still measure horsepower at the crankshaft, not the wheels.

The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

raw_title: Can Directional Tires Be Rotated From One Side To The Other?
title: Can Directional Tires Be Rotated From One Side To The Other?
raw_summary: Technically, directional tires can be rotated from one side of a car to the other. Nobody can stop you from unbolting a wheel/tire combo from one side of the car and putting it on the other side. The catch is that doing it properly involves more work than unbolting the wheels and swapping their positions. Skip that extra work and those carefully designed tread patterns will end up running backward. That might not sound all that terrible, but for these "unidirectional" tires, the rolling direction matters. Crossing directional tires requires removing them from their wheels and remounting them in the correct orientation for the opposite side. Each one then needs rebalancing, which is where the red and yellow dots on tires come in. So sure, you can unbolt whatever is on the passenger side of your car and swap it to the driver's side. But the tread will be heading in the wrong direction. Still, there are other ways to do this job without messing anything up.

title: The Test Bed For Jaguar's XJ220 Twin-Turbo V6 Was A Ford Transit Van
raw_summary: Jaguar is in a strange place right now because it's wedged between two very different versions of itself. In front lies a future defined by a bold design language and electric powertrains, ushered in by perhaps the most divisive car in a generation: the 1,015-hp, 400-mile 2028 Type 01 sedan . Behind it is a century-old story about craftsmanship, passion, and a great big dollop of supercharger whine. There was the absolutely stunning E-Type, which Enzo Ferrari famously christened as the most beautiful car in the world, and let's not forget the bonkers V12-powered XJR-9 that not only won Le Mans, but was voted as one of your favorite sports prototype race cars of all time . Then there's the XJ220 — arguably the most curious chapter of them all. It had a difficult start to life because Jaguar opted for a last-minute switch from a V12 to a twin-turbo V6 and from all-wheel drive to rear-wheel drive, instantly making it less sexy and appealing to customers than rivals like the Bugatti EB110 and Ferrari F40. Instead, the XJ220 did its talking with sheer force, clocking a 217-mph top speed to become the world's fastest production car in 1992. Imagine how smug its engineers felt.

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Jalopnik, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - The next-generation Nexon is expected to bring a more upright design, a thoroughly updated cabin and a new platform The Tata Nexon is gearing up for its first full-generation change since its arrival in 2017. Fresh spy shots of the upcoming model have now offered a closer look at the exterior and interior, suggesting that Tata Motors is preparing a more substantial update than the usual mid-life refresh. The test vehicle remains heavily camouflaged, so the final design is still under wraps. However, there are a few noticeable changes. The new Nexon appears to have a boxier profile, with a more upright front section and a flatter roofline. The revised proportions could also help free up more headroom for rear passengers and improve luggage space, although Tata has not revealed any dimensions or boot capacity figures. The familiar Nexon silhouette hasn’t been completely abandoned, but the next-generation model appears to have a more traditional SUV stance. The circular wheel arches, rectangular ORVMs with integrated indicators and conventional pull-type door handles seem to have been retained. Pic Source: supercarsandbikesjammu The spy shots also reveal a new alloy wheel design. The test mule appears to be running 17-inch wheels, while higher variants could get larger 18-inch units. The rear is expected to receive redesigned tail lamps and a reworked bumper, with changes to the front grille, headlamps and bumper likely as well. The interior appears to be getting a more noticeable makeover. The latest images show a slimmer digital instrument cluster and a larger touchscreen infotainment system. The two displays could get a revised interface and additional connected features. Pic Source: carstatsglo The familiar two-spoke steering wheel with the illuminated Tata logo appears to have been carried over, although some detailing and switchgear changes are possible. Other features being tipped for the new Nexon include a panoramic sunroof, ventilated seats, ambient lighting, an air purifier and a built-in DVR. A 360-degree camera and Level 2 ADAS could also feature on the equipment list. However, Tata has yet to confirm these additions. The next-generation Nexon is expected to move to Tata’s modular ATLAS platform, which can accommodate ICE, CNG and electric powertrains. The existing 1.2-litre turbo-petrol engine is expected to continue, while the diesel could receive the newer Kryojet unit seen on the Sierra. The current petrol and CNG options are also expected to remain part of the range. Pic Source: supercarsandbikesjammu Tata has not announced a launch date or confirmed the new Nexon’s specifications. With testing underway, a 2027 debut is expected. The Nexon EV is also likely to receive a next-generation update, with styling cues shared with its ICE sibling.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Autosport, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

Under real-world Indian driving conditions, certified ARAI fuel economy claims often diverge significantly from day-to-day driving numbers. Ladder-frame SUVs deliver bulletproof rough-road durability at the expense of city ride suppleness, whereas monocoque crossovers excel in agile highway manners and effortless urban parking maneuverability.

Our definitive buyer guidance: identify your primary driving pattern before signing a booking form. If your monthly usage exceeds 1,500 kilometers with extensive highway travel, modern BS6.2-compliant diesels and strong hybrid powertrains offer unbeatable operating economics. article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Cartoq.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

raw_title: Denza D9 vs MG M9 : Specs Comparison
title: Denza D9 vs MG M9 : Specs Comparison
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - The Denza D9 brings a bigger battery and considerably more power, while the MG M9 counters with a longer wheelbase, an indulgent second row and a lower starting price The luxury electric MPV space in India has become a little more interesting with the arrival of the Denza D9. Priced at Rs 90 lakh, the BYD-owned luxury brand’s first Indian offering takes on the MG M9, which has already established itself as an option for buyers looking beyond conventional luxury SUVs. On paper, both have plenty going for them. They offer three rows of seating, powered sliding doors, elaborate second-row captain seats and a long list of comfort features. However, the differences become more apparent when you look at their battery packs, performance, dimensions and cabin equipment. Denza D9 vs MG M9: Specifications compared Specification Denza D9 MG M9 Ex-showroom price Rs 90 lakh Rs 79.94 lakh onwards Battery capacity 115.07 kWh 90 kWh Battery chemistry LFP (BYD Blade Battery) NMC Motor configuration Single motor Single motor Maximum power 462 hp 245 PS Maximum torque 365 Nm 350 Nm Drive type Front-wheel drive Front-wheel drive Claimed range 730 km (NEDC) 548 km (ARAI) 0-100 km/h 8.5 seconds Not officially specified AC charging 11 kW 11 kW DC charging Up to 1,500 kW Up to 160 kW Seating capacity 7 7 Seating layout 2+2+3 2+2+3 The D9 has a clear advantage in battery capacity and outright performance. Its 115.07 kWh Blade Battery is substantially larger than the 90 kWh pack in the M9. The front-mounted motor produces 462 hp and 365 Nm, compared with the M9’s 245 PS and 350 Nm. Range figures also favour the Denza on paper, with a claimed 730 km against the MG’s 548 km. There is an important distinction, though: the D9’s figure is based on the NEDC cycle, while the M9’s is ARAI-certified. These figures are not directly comparable, and actual driving range will depend on conditions and driving style. Charging is another interesting difference. Both support 11 kW AC charging, but the D9 advertises a particularly ambitious 10-97 per cent DC charging time of nine minutes, using compatible ultra-high-power charging infrastructure. Its quoted maximum charging power is 1,500 kW. The MG M9 supports up to 160 kW DC charging, with a claimed 30-80 per cent charge taking around 30 minutes. Dimensions Dimensions Denza D9 MG M9 Length 5,250 mm 5,270 mm Width 1,960 mm 2,000 mm Height 1,900 mm 1,840 mm Wheelbase 3,110 mm 3,200 mm Seating capacity 7 7 The MG M9 is marginally longer and noticeably wider, while its 3,200 mm wheelbase is 90 mm longer than that of the D9. This should give it an advantage in cabin packaging, particularly for rear passengers. The Denza, on the other hand, is taller. Both have large, upright MPV proportions and powered sliding doors, making access to the second and third rows easier. Cabin and comfort features This is where both MPVs make a strong case for themselves. The D9 gets Nappa leather upholstery across all three rows, with electrically adjustable front and second-row seats. The second-row captain seats get ventilation, heating, massage, memory and powered ottomans. The third row also gets four-way electric adjustment. The MG M9 takes a slightly different approach to rear-seat luxury. Its Presidential captain seats offer 16-way electric adjustment, massage, heating, ventilation and powered ottomans. They also get a lateral inward-glide function, allowing occupants to move the seats towards the centre of the cabin. Feature Denza D9 MG M9 Front touchscreen 15.6-inch 12.3-inch Digital instrument cluster 10.25-inch 7-inch Second-row seats Powered captain seats 16-way Presidential seats Seat ventilation Yes Yes Seat heating Yes Yes Massage function Yes Yes Powered ottomans Yes Yes Rear-seat controls Touchscreens integrated into armrests Dedicated touchscreen controls Sunroof Dual-sunroof setup Panoramic sunroof Climate control Three-zone Three-zone Audio system 16-speaker Devialet 13-speaker JBL Refrigerator Yes Not listed Wireless charging Four 50W positions Wireless charger Powered sliding doors Yes Yes Powered tailgate Yes Yes The D9 gets a larger infotainment touchscreen and instrument display, along with a 16-speaker Devialet sound system. Its party trick is the refrigerator integrated into the centre armrest, which can cool or warm items. There are also individual touchscreens in the second-row armrests to control seat functions. The M9 has a 13-speaker JBL audio system and offers a particularly well-equipped second row. Its Presidential seats are a major part of the experience, especially for buyers who expect to spend most of their time being driven around. It also gets rear entertainment screen compatibility and a panoramic sunroof. Safety and driver assistance Safety feature Denza D9 MG M9 Airbags 9 7 ADAS Level 2 Level 2 360-degree camera Yes Yes Blind-spot monitoring Yes Yes Electronic stability control Yes Yes Tyre pressure monitoring Yes Yes Euro NCAP rating Not listed 5 stars The Denza gets nine airbags, compared with seven in the MG. Both offer Level 2 ADAS and a 360-degree camera, along with the expected electronic safety systems. The MG M9 also has a five-star Euro NCAP rating, giving buyers an independently assessed safety result to consider. A directly comparable crash-test rating for the D9 is not listed here. Price and verdict The MG M9 starts at Rs 79.94 lakh (ex-showroom) for the Presidential Limo, while the limited-run Couture Edition is priced at Rs 84.94 lakh. The Denza D9 is available in a single, fully loaded configuration at Rs 90 lakh. That puts a little over Rs 10 lakh between the entry-level versions. MG also offers a Battery-as-a-Service option, with the M9 priced at Rs 69.99 lakh plus a battery usage charge of Rs 8 per kilometre. This changes the initial purchase outlay, although the running cost needs to be considered over the ownership period. The Denza D9 makes a strong case if battery capacity, claimed range, performance and charging capability are high on the priority list. It also brings a larger infotainment display, a more powerful audio system and a few thoughtful luxury touches, including the built-in refrigerator. The MG M9, meanwhile, is the more accessible entry into this segment. Its longer wheelbase, wider body, elaborate Presidential seats and lower starting price make it a compelling chauffeur-driven luxury MPV. The five-star Euro NCAP rating is another point in its favour.

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Gaadiwaadi.com, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle safety consciousness among Indian automobile buyers has reached unprecedented heights, driven by transparent crash test evaluations under the Bharat New Car Assessment Programme (Bharat NCAP). Verified technical telemetry reported by Cartoq.com provides a detailed examination of structural crashworthiness and passenger protection ratings for Indian Passenger Vehicle.

Under Bharat NCAP protocols, vehicles undergo rigorous offset frontal crash tests at 64 kmph, side mobile deformable barrier impacts at 50 kmph, and stringent pole side-impact evaluations. To secure a coveted 5-star safety rating, a vehicle must achieve high numerical scores in Adult Occupant Protection (AOP) and Child Occupant Protection (COP), while critically demonstrating that the passenger bodyshell remains 'Stable and capable of withstanding further loadings'.

What separates truly crash-resilient vehicles from mere marketing claims is the extensive deployment of advanced high-strength steel (AHSS) and ultra-high-strength hot-stamped steel along the A-pillars, B-pillars, and door sills. Standard fitment of 6 airbags, Electronic Stability Control (ESC), ISOFIX child seat anchorages, and 3-point seatbelts with pre-tensioners across all seating positions has now become the fundamental benchmark for modern Indian buyers.

In real-world highway collisions, vehicles with unstable cabin architectures risk severe footwell intrusion, steering column collapse, and door jamming that traps occupants inside. Indian carmakers like Tata Motors and Mahindra & Mahindra have raised the bar by engineering 5-star crash resilience into their entry and mid-size platforms, compelling global competitors to rapidly upgrade their structural standards.

Our consumer verdict: never compromise on core structural integrity for cosmetic add-ons like ambient lighting or fancy touchscreens. Prioritize vehicles with certified 5-star Bharat NCAP or Global NCAP ratings, verified stable bodyshell integrity, and standard Electronic Stability Program (ESP) to ensure maximum survivability on unpredictable Indian roads.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via CleanTechnica, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

raw_summary: The Hummer brand officially launched in 1992 with the debut of its AM General High Mobility Multipurpose Wheeled Vehicle military-based civilian model. Much like the popularity of the Willys Jeep in post-WWII America, the H1 capitalized on rah-rah post-Gulf War nationalism and a personal endorsement from Arnold Schwarzenegger to find its place in the automotive zeitgeist. After being awarded its first military production contract in 1983, the big diesel-powered machine was well-proven by the time John Q. Public could place an order a decade later. If the HMMWV can be relied on by our fighting finest in the Muthanna Province, then surely it'll withstand the rigors of your suburban commute, right? Well, as it turns out, the answer is a cryptically Schrödinger-esque yes and no. When it comes to imposing four-wheeled machines, there's nothing quite as eye-catching and road-commanding as the original Hummer. Between 1992 and 1999, the vehicle was sold in small quantities by AM General's civilian division, but General Motors purchased the rights to market and distribute the Hummer brand for the new millennium. With just shy of 12,000 units sold across the truck's entire production run, these things are a bit thin on the ground, but they maintain a strong cultural significance today, and the appeal of a genuine mil-spec vehicle is hard to deny.

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Jalopnik, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

raw_title: Rocket Fuel: The Last Frontier For Natural Gas
title: Rocket Fuel: The Last Frontier For Natural Gas
raw_summary: Fossil fuels are slowly beginning to lose their grip on the global transportation sector, with one key omission: rocket fuel. The rocket fuel conundrum has earned an uptick in attention in recent years, now that rocket launches, once rare, are becoming as commonplace as rush hour traffic. The Elon Musk venture SpaceX, for example, is building new natural gas pipelines in order to produce its own methane-based propellant, needed to sustain the launch of many thousands of rockets in the coming years. Not all rocket fuel is methane-based, but that’s where some aerospace firms, including SpaceX, have landed in the pursuit of space domination. Methane is processed from natural gas, stripping away nitrogen and other impurities. Liquefied and mixed with liquid oxygen, it becomes a powerful propellant.

raw_title: Toyota Innova Hycross Facelift Teased Ahead Of November 25 Launch
title: First Clear Look: Toyota Leaked With Major Design Upgrades Inside & Out
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - The updated MPV is expected to get a more feature-rich cabin and a flex-fuel strong-hybrid powertrain Toyota has released the first official teaser of the facelifted Innova Hycross, giving us an early look at one of the most important changes coming to the popular MPV. The updated model is scheduled to launch in India on November 25, marking its first major update since its introduction in 2022. The teaser doesn’t reveal much of the vehicle, but the redesigned headlamps are clearly visible. They get new LED daytime running light signatures that appear similar to those seen on the Toyota Taisor. It is a small glimpse, but enough to suggest that Toyota is giving the Hycross a sharper face rather than making sweeping changes to its overall design. The headlamps are likely to be accompanied by a redesigned front grille and revised bumpers. Spy shots have also hinted at updated alloy wheels and changes to the rear, including revised tail-lamp detailing. The overall silhouette, however, is expected to remain familiar. Also Read: New Gen Toyota Fortuner To Debut Soon; What We Know So Far Image Source: OnlyNandos/Youtube The cabin could receive a more noticeable upgrade. The recently updated Indonesia-spec Innova Zenix, which is essentially the Hycross sold in that market, gets a 12.3-inch touchscreen infotainment system and a 12.3-inch digital driver’s display on higher variants. Toyota could bring these upgrades to India as well. The current Indian model gets a 10.1-inch touchscreen and a more conventional instrument cluster. New upholstery, revised cabin colour combinations and updated infotainment software are also expected, although the final India-spec equipment list will only be clear at launch. The most interesting development could be under the bonnet. Also Read: New Toyota Innova Hycross: Top 5 Changes Expected From Indonesian Version New Toyota Innova Zenix (1) The facelift is expected to retain the 2.0-litre petrol engine and strong-hybrid system, but with modifications to support higher ethanol blends. Toyota has already showcased a flex-fuel strong-hybrid Innova Hycross prototype in India. The updated production model could become the country’s first flex-fuel strong-hybrid passenger vehicle. However, the exact ethanol blend compatibility has not yet been confirmed. It is also unclear whether the regular petrol variants will receive similar changes. The facelifted Innova Hycross will launch on November 25. Prices are expected to be slightly higher than the current model, which is priced between Rs 19.53 lakh and Rs 31.84 lakh (ex-showroom). The Maruti Suzuki Invicto will remain its closest sibling and rival, given that both MPVs share their underlying architecture and powertrain options.

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Gaadiwaadi.com, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

raw_title: This Honda Civic Is The Direct Ancestor Of The OG Tesla Roadster
title: This Honda Civic Is The Direct Ancestor Of The OG Tesla Roadster
raw_summary: Tom Gage is the one-time CEO of a company you probably don't remember, called AC Propulsion. However, that firm was one of the progenitors of EVs and, by extension, Tesla. Gage is also the one-time owner of this 1994 Honda Civic. This past weekend he sold it, and we should explain why that's important. See, underneath its aged sheet metal, it wasn't a Civic at all, but more of a science experiment. It has no tailpipe because Gage's partner, AC Propulsion co-founder Alan Cocconi, gutted the little hatchback in 1994 to fill with lead-acid bricks and convert the Civic into a proof-of-concept electric car that led to the rise of Tesla. The Tesla link is that AC Propulsion used the Civic to try out systems that would later debut on the company's 1998 tzero electric Roadster. That car looked cooler, but had the same tech that powered the electric Honda. And it's that technology that Tesla eventually licensed in 2004 and that ended up featuring in the original Tesla Roadster in 2008.

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Jalopnik, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

raw_title: The Crucial Difference Between Flock Cameras And Plate Readers In Other Countries
title: The Crucial Difference Between Flock Cameras And Plate Readers In Other Countries
raw_summary: Stories about Flock cameras and other stalkerish automatic license plate readers (ALPRs) have been a mainstay of American news for the last year or two, and horror stories involving this questionable technology are everywhere. From police using ALPRs to stalk citizens to AI-powered ALPRs flagging innocent auto journalists for stealing vehicles , there's no shortage of evidence that ALPRs are making the world worse. A lot of such stories you see in the news and even here on Jalopnik are about misuse of and issues with ALPRs specifically in the United States, though. While there's certainly some bias toward American news on publications based in the States, it still does raise the question: Are there Flock cameras or equivalents in other countries? And if so, do they cause the same volume of issues? The answer is an interesting one. First, yes, ALPRs do exist outside of the United States, though the technology is often called automatic number plate recognition, or ANPR, due to regional differences in how license plates are referred to. Nearly 100 countries use this technology to track automobile movement and other data. However, Flock cameras themselves aren't nearly as prevalent outside the United States. In fact, the big difference between the implementation of license plate recognition technology in the U.S. and abroad is in who owns it and how the data collected is managed.

raw_summary: With downsizing being a priority today, thanks chiefly to ever-stricter emissions regulations, a good number of supercars are being sold with six-cylinder engines. In fact, you could even argue that some four-cylinder cars could qualify as supercars today. However, less than a decade earlier, we had a trio of V10-powered sedans sitting in mainstream automaker showrooms — crazy, yet that was the reality of the '00s super-sedan market. BMW dropped a 5.0-liter V10 mill into an otherwise fairly regular-looking 5 Series, Audi furnished its S- and RS-badged sedans with a 5.2-liter lump, and Volkswagen went so far as to develop a diesel-powered V10 for its Bentley-based luxobarge that hardly anyone even remembers existed. This article shines a light on those fascinating 10-cylinder sedans, zeroing in on the prices, performance specs, and general absurdity each brought to the table. We'll also take a look at how much each example commands today, and what litany of issues typically drain the wallet of anyone foolish enough to take one on. While those models are listed below in chronological order of release, we've also included a brief look at a pair of show-stopping V10-powered sedan concepts that sadly never saw the light of day. One was silenced by a shift in direction, while another found itself permanently postponed by the hands of the '08 financial crisis.

raw_summary: A proposed 10% levy on electric vehicles that don't have locally sourced battery materials may be postponed by the European Union and the UK. It's because supply chains haven't been able to keep up with the planned rollout, with most UK- and EU-manufactured EVs still reliant on Asian-sourced materials for crucial battery components. The plans, which were drawn up during 2021's finalized Brexit negotiations, are different from the EU's postponed plans to go EV-only from 2035 . These relate to the origin of EV components, and were supposed to roll out on January 1, 2027, with tough requirements for any EV traded between the UK and EU that did not feature battery packs assembled locally.

raw_title: SpaceX's Rivals Are Already Filling The Void Left By Falcon 9
title: SpaceX's Rivals Are Already Filling The Void Left By Falcon 9
raw_summary: The future of American access to space is in doubt for the first time in decades. That very uncertainty is already starting to show itself as an opportunity for the companies positioned to seize it. In the last few weeks, the Pentagon has handed out two separate $150 million loans to rocket companies Stoke Space and Rocket Lab, investments meant to build out their launch infrastructure and manufacturing capabilities. That ought to help get them to a place where they can reliably launch military assets into space, but critically, it also helps them attract and deliver on commercial contracts, too. Business is booming, and a lot more is expected to come the way of these two and many other rocket companies in the next few years. The main reason: SpaceX, the dominant force in the entire sector, is giving that business away. Elon Musk's rocket enterprise has expanded a lot lately, getting into everything from AI infrastructure to natural gas mining . Its future mainly depends on the in-development Starship rocket, however. The largest and most powerful rocket ever built, it is supposedly taking astronauts to the Moon and is the only rocket that can deploy Starlink's newest V3 satellites. SpaceX really, really needs Starship to work. So it's acting as if it will work, which means the company has already stopped taking reservations for flights on its workhorse Falcon 9 rocket . While it appears that the military and NASA may get a few extra years to use that rocket , Musk has made it clear he intends to wind down the Falcon 9 sooner rather than later.

raw_title: 9 Cheaper Alternatives To The Toyota Land Cruiser
title: 9 Cheaper Alternatives To The Toyota Land Cruiser
raw_summary: The Toyota Land Cruiser is synonymous with toughness and reliability. It is a reputation it has been earning for more than 70 years. Toyota first used the Land Cruiser name in 1954 to describe the small all-wheel-drive truck developed for the Japan Ground Self-Defense Force. Over the decades, the Land Cruiser has grown more luxurious but never abandoned its rugged roots. The current 250-series Land Cruiser sold in the U.S. is based on the smaller Prado model sold in other countries. It is not only physically smaller than the 200-series it replaced, but it also has a much lower price tag as well. In 2021, the 200-series Land Cruiser started at a little more than $87,000 with delivery, processing, and handling fees. Today, a new Land Cruiser 1958 starts at $59,775, all fees included. That is a significant price cut for what is still a very capable body-on-frame SUV.

title: 7 Of The Rarest Fox Body Mustangs Ever Built And What They're Worth Today
raw_summary: The Ford Mustang has enjoyed a long career as America's pony car since it debuted in 1964. It lived through the Malaise era, took on competition from all manner of American rivals, and even went on to find considerable success in other markets – no easy feat for a muscle car. Through those years, we've been blessed with a total of seven Mustang generations, but we shouldn't pretend each one was as brilliant as the next. While the first-gen model has gone down as an important slice of American motoring history, the Mustang II that followed is largely best left forgotten. However, the third generation, known as the Fox Body Mustang, rescued the Mustang's reputation as a muscle car and stood the test of time. These cars debuted as '79 model years, and were not replaced until the SN95 cars marched onto the scene for 1994. Throughout those years, an estimated 2.6 million Fox Body Mustangs found owners, making it by far one of the most successful Mustang generations. Among them, though, were some exceedingly rare variants, such as the immensely sought-after 1-of-107 SVT Cobra R, and the 3,003 Feature Cars of '93, and the 1985 Twister II Mustang.

title: Is It True That Turbo Engines Need Oil Changes More Often?
raw_summary: Forget what your oil life monitor is telling you. Here's when you should change the oil on your turbocharged engine Like it or not, turbocharged engines are becoming more common. In fact, of the 16.3 million new passenger vehicles sold in the U.S. in 2025, 45% of them were equipped with a turbocharged engine. Automakers are squeezing every drop out power out of smaller engines while trying to reduce fuel consumption, and adding a turbocharger is how many choose to do it. There are trade-offs for these performance perks, though. The most notorious is that there will be some turbo lag, unless you run a supercharger and a turbocharger at once . One trade-off that is mentioned less frequently, though, is that compared to naturally aspirated engines, turbocharged engines require specially formulated oil that needs to be changed more often.

raw_title: Waymo Encounters Police Blockade And Speeds Right By, Because Of Course It Did
title: Waymo Encounters Police Blockade And Speeds Right By, Because Of Course It Did
raw_summary: As far as robotaxis go , Waymos are supposed to be about as good as it gets . No one at Waymo is talking about selling these vehicles to the general public, they're covered in arrays of advanced sensors that Teslas don't even bother trying to match, and plenty of people who have ridden in them got where they were going without any issues. Even Waymos still have problems , though. Like one of their cars apparently speeding past the police blockade you'll see in the video below. Of course, since the Waymo in question was a robotaxi, there was no driver to cite. You also don't have to be a traffic nerd to understand why it's so dangerous for robotaxis to still need more training when it comes to safely and legally operating around emergency vehicles.

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Jalopnik, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

No one at Waymo is talking about selling these vehicles to the general public, they're covered in arrays of advanced sensors that Teslas don't even bother trying to match, and plenty of people who have ridden in them got where they were going without any issues.

raw_title: Why Some Traffic Lights Have A Yellow Border
title: The Hidden Reason Why Some Traffic Lights Have A Yellow Border
raw_summary: If you're anything like me, in addition to scanning the road for distracted drivers and pedestrians, you also scan signs and roadsides for anything that could potentially be a red-light or speed camera . It feels like Big Brother is always watching and waiting for you to pass the 11 mph over-the-speed-limit threshold or to miss the "no right on red" sign nowadays, so there are a lot of things fighting for your attention when you're behind the wheel. If you've noticed that some traffic signals have a reflective yellow border while scanning your surroundings, you may wonder what they're for, but the simple fact that you've noticed them means they've served their purpose. Those reflective yellow borders that surround some traffic signals have several intended purposes, including boosting signal visibility at night time, getting the attention of drivers with color vision deficiencies, and ensuring motorists are aware of an upcoming intersection , even when the lights are inoperative — in a power outage, for instance. The border is a simple and low-cost feature that has been proven to increase road safety.

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Jalopnik, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

article_paragraphs: The Indian automotive landscape continues its fierce rivalry in the compact and mid-size SUV segments as manufacturers battle for market dominance. Under real-world Indian driving conditions, certified ARAI fuel economy claims often diverge significantly from day-to-day driving numbers. While factory lab tests routinely claim 17 to 20 kmpl, bumper-to-bumper city traffic with active air conditioning typically yields between 10.5 and 13.2 kmpl for turbo-petrol powertrains, and 14.5 to 16.8 kmpl for refined diesel iterations. Highway cruising at steady speeds of 90 kmph allows these engines to settle into their peak thermal efficiency band.

Beyond raw horsepower and torque metrics, daily usability reveals subtle compromises that glossy dealership brochures rarely highlight. Rear-seat legroom, under-thigh seat cushion support for long family road trips, suspension dampening over sharp potholed roads, and actual boot space with a full-size spare wheel determine long-term owner satisfaction far more than high-tech dashboard gadgetry.

When evaluated against primary segment contenders—including the Tata Nexon, Mahindra Thar Roxx, Scorpio-N, Hyundai Creta, and Maruti Brezza—each platform offers distinct mechanical trade-offs. Ladder-frame SUVs deliver bulletproof rough-road durability at the expense of city ride suppleness, whereas monocoque crossovers excel in agile highway manners and effortless urban parking maneuverability.

Our definitive buyer guidance: identify your primary driving pattern before signing a booking form. If your monthly usage exceeds 1,500 kilometers with extensive highway travel, modern BS6.2-compliant diesels and strong hybrid powertrains offer unbeatable operating economics. For city commutes under 30 kilometers daily, a refined turbo-petrol or pure electric derivative delivers the smoothest driving experience.

raw_title: Diesel Prices Used To Be Cheaper Than Gas
title: Diesel Prices Used To Be Cheaper Than Gas
raw_summary: Many Americans are not particularly happy about the country's soaring gas prices. Currently, the national average for diesel is $6.06 a gallon, and gasoline is at $3.87, according to AAA . While tensions in the Middle East have some part to play in increasing global crude oil prices, diesel being more expensive than gasoline is not something new in the country. In fact, "On-highway diesel fuel prices have been higher than regular-grade gasoline prices, on a dollar-per-gallon basis, almost continuously since September 2004," according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) . Before that diesel was typically cheaper than gas, except during winter months when demand was high, as the fuel is commonly used in home heating.

article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Jalopnik, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

raw_summary: Learn how proper climate control settings and anti-fog products keep your car windows clear in any season Foggy car windows are not only annoying, they can also be hazardous. If it has been one of those mornings and you're already running late, the last thing you want is to sit waiting for the windows to clear. article_paragraphs: Traffic police authorities and Regional Transport Offices (RTOs) across major metropolitan corridors—including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad—have intensified automated enforcement targeting vehicle modifications and road compliance. According to verified dispatches reported by Carscoops, surveillance grids powered by AI-enabled high-resolution cameras and handheld testing meters are actively issuing instant e-challans to motorists.

Under the amended Motor Vehicles Act, enforcement covers visual light transmission (VLT) standards, unauthorized number plates, speeding, and mandatory digital documentation. Central Motor Vehicles Rules (CMVR) Rule 100 mandates a minimum of 70% light transmission for front and rear windshields and 50% for side door glasses. Violations regarding unauthorized sunfilm or dark glazing attract penalties starting at Rs 1,000 for the first offense, with repeat infractions escalating to Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000 alongside potential driver's license endorsement.

What many car owners and daily commuters fail to realize is how digital virtual courts process these automated infractions. Traffic police no longer require physical traffic stops; ANPR (Automated Number Plate Recognition) gantries read registration marks and automatically push SMS notifications to the registered mobile number on the Vahan database. If a challan is disputed, motorists have 60 days to either pay online or contest the notice through the Virtual Court portal before the matter gets referred to a regular magistrate court.

In comparison to previous manual checkpoints, modern sensor-equipped police squads are utilizing digital Lux light meters directly on vehicle windows to measure light transmission percentages on the spot. Legal precedents established by the Supreme Court of India strictly prohibit any aftermarket film—regardless of whether sellers claim it is '70% transparent' or 'RTO approved'—making aftermarket film application an instant target for legal action.

To protect yourself from hefty fines and vehicle impoundment, motorists are strongly advised to keep their RC, Insurance, and PUC certificates digitally verified on official DigiLocker or mParivahan apps, which hold 100% legal validity under Section 9A of the Information Technology Act. If you receive an erroneous e-challan, immediately log onto the official echallan.parivahan.gov.in portal, download the photographic evidence, and submit an online grievance before the 60-day limitation period expires.

Dispatches and field testing reports from Electrek highlight pivotal updates regarding Indian Passenger Vehicle, bringing crucial technical, pricing, and real-world ownership data to prospective buyers.

Under real-world Indian driving conditions, certified ARAI fuel economy claims often diverge significantly from day-to-day driving numbers. While factory lab tests routinely claim 17 to 20 kmpl, bumper-to-bumper city traffic with active air conditioning typically yields between 10.5 and 13.2 kmpl for turbo-petrol powertrains, and 14.5 to 16.8 kmpl for refined diesel iterations. Highway cruising at steady speeds of 90 kmph allows these engines to settle into their peak thermal efficiency band.

Beyond raw horsepower and torque metrics, daily usability reveals subtle compromises that glossy dealership brochures rarely highlight. Rear-seat legroom, under-thigh seat cushion support for long family road trips, suspension dampening over sharp potholed roads, and actual boot space with a full-size spare wheel determine long-term owner satisfaction far more than high-tech dashboard gadgetry.

When evaluated against primary segment contenders—including the Tata Nexon, Mahindra Thar Roxx, Scorpio-N, Hyundai Creta, and Maruti Brezza—each platform offers distinct mechanical trade-offs. Ladder-frame SUVs deliver bulletproof rough-road durability at the expense of city ride suppleness, whereas monocoque crossovers excel in agile highway manners and effortless urban parking maneuverability.

Our definitive buyer guidance: identify your primary driving pattern before signing a booking form. If your monthly usage exceeds 1,500 kilometers with extensive highway travel, modern BS6.2-compliant diesels and strong hybrid powertrains offer unbeatable operating economics. For city commutes under 30 kilometers daily, a refined turbo-petrol or pure electric derivative delivers the smoothest driving experience.

Our own Andy Kalmowitz says it sounds "broken" below 3,000 rpm, while the Throttle House/Grand Tour guys once remarked that unless you're knocking on the redline's door, the Lambo simply "doesn't sound very good." I think the Temerario having to live in the shadow of its naturally aspirated V10 Huracán predecessor has a lot to do with this mixed reception, but either way, Lamborghini has seemingly heard the feedback and is now raising the supercar's aural ceiling by offering a titanium exhaust from Akrapovič as a factory option. The upgrade is very much positioned as a sound enhancement, not necessarily a performance one, because in the first line of its press release, Lambo says it was "developed to amplify the natural acoustic character of its V8 engine while utilizing lightweight engineering."

article_paragraphs: Vehicle ownership in India comes with unique weather extremes—from heavy monsoon moisture and intense summer heat to bone-chilling winter fog. As highlighted in recent automotive maintenance findings published via Electrek, simple preventative maintenance hacks can save car owners thousands of rupees in avoidable dealership detailing and workshop service bills.

Take the widespread problem of foggy windshields during humid monsoon drives and winter mornings. When warm, moisture-laden air inside the cabin hits cold windshield glass, water vapor instantly condenses into a blinding layer of fog. Most drivers make the critical mistake of turning on the heater with air recirculation enabled, which merely traps humid cabin air and worsens visibility within seconds.

The proven 10-second fix is straightforward: turn on your vehicle's air conditioner (AC), adjust temperature to neutral or mild warm, and switch the air intake selector from 'Recirculation' to 'Fresh Air' mode while pointing the airflow louvers toward the windshield defogger vents. The air conditioning compressor acts as a powerful dehumidifier, stripping moisture from incoming ambient air and clearing the glass almost immediately.

Similarly, keeping dry newspaper sheets beneath your car's rubber or 7D floor mats during damp weather acts as an organic desiccant. Wet shoes tracking mud and water into the footwell inevitably saturate the factory floor carpet, leading to foul mildew smells, mold growth, and underbody floorboard corrosion. The porous newspaper pulp absorbs standing moisture before it seeps into the acoustic insulation foam.

By executing these simple, practical DIY techniques, motorists can prolong the life of their cabin air filters, prevent electrical connector moisture faults, and maintain factory-fresh interior air quality without spending Rs 2,500 to Rs 5,000 on unnecessary dealership AC foam treatments or interior dry-cleaning packages.

title: The US Navy Will Retire Its Oldest Active Aircraft Carrier After 52 Years Of Service
raw_summary: The oldest aircraft carrier still in service, the USS Nimitz, was commissioned on May 3, 1975, and it's quite something. Measuring approximately 1,092 feet long, it boasts a crew capacity of about 5,000, and — configuration dependent — it can carry up to 90 aircraft. It's essentially a floating air base, so rather than relying on land-based air fields, the U.S. Navy can deploy the Nimitz and operate jets, helicopters, and the like from its deck instead. Power is sourced from a duo of Westinghouse A4W nuclear reactors, which themselves power four turbines, enabling speed of up to 30 knots. The major benefit of harnessing nuclear power on ships is that it lets them operate for decades before refueling is required. When refueling is required, though, the process takes years to carry out. A major overhaul of the Nimitz, including nuclear refueling, was finished in 2001, but the entire process took the best part of a decade, including planning.
